questions.stem:
(a) Conductivity of \(2 \times 10^{-3}\) M methanoic acid is \(8 \times 10^{-5}\) S \(\mathrm{cm^{-1}}\). Calculate its molar conductivity and degree of dissociation if \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}^{\mathrm{o}}\) for methanoic acid is 404 S \(\mathrm{cm^2 mol^{-1}}\).
(b) Calculate the \(\Delta_{\mathrm{r}}\mathrm{G}^{\circ}\) and log \(\mathrm{K_c}\) for the given reaction at 298 K :
\(\mathrm{Ni_{(s)}} + 2\mathrm{Ag^+_{(aq)}} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Ni^{2+}_{(aq)}} + 2\mathrm{Ag_{(s)}}\)
Given : \(\mathrm{E^{\circ}_{Ni^{2+}/Ni}} = -0.25\) V, \(\mathrm{E^{o}_{Ag^+/Ag}} = +0.80\) V
\(1\mathrm{F} = 96500\) C \(\mathrm{mol^{-1}}\).
questions._flag: NO 'OR' is printed between (a) and (b) — verified on the English page (idx 20) and on the Hindi facing page (idx 19) — so this is ONE 5-mark question in two parts. The printed '3 + 2' therefore splits (a)=3 and (b)=2, which the marking scheme confirms (½+½+1+½+½ for (a), ½×4 for (b)). This is the same shape as Q26, and the paper's own internal-choice count corroborates it: instruction (viii) promises 2 choices in Section E and both are already accounted for by Q34 and Q35. Part (b) is a \(\Delta_{\mathrm{r}}\mathrm{G}^{\circ} = -n\mathrm{F}\mathrm{E}^{\circ}_{\mathrm{cell}}\) / log-\(\mathrm{K_c}\) calculation belonging to 'Nernst Equation'; the row is filed on 'Conductance of Electrolytic Solutions' for the 3-mark part (a).

questions.subtopic: General Properties of the Transition Elements (d-Block)
questions.stem:
(I) Account for the following :
(i) \(\mathrm{E^o}\) value for \(\mathrm{Mn^{3+}/Mn^{2+}}\) couple is much more positive than that for \(\mathrm{Cr^{3+}/Cr^{2+}}\).
(ii) \(\mathrm{Sc^{3+}}\) is colourless whereas \(\mathrm{Ti^{3+}}\) is coloured in an aqueous solution.
(iii) Actinoids show wide range of oxidation states.
(II) Write the chemical equations for the preparation of \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\) from \(\mathrm{MnO_2}\).
questions._flag: The printed marks are '3 + 2'. Part (I) carries 3 marks and is mostly general d-block behaviour, so the row is filed on 'General Properties of the Transition Elements (d-Block)'; within it (I)(iii) is 'The Actinoids', and the 2-mark part (II) is 'Some Important Compounds of Transition Elements'.

questions.stem:

(i) Transition metals form alloys.
(ii) \(\mathrm{Ce^{4+}}\) is a strong oxidising agent.
(II) Write one similarity and one difference between chemistry of Lanthanoids and Actinoids.
(III) Complete the following ionic equation :
\(\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}} + 2\mathrm{OH^-} \longrightarrow\)
questions._flag: The printed marks are '2 + 2 + 1'. Filed on 'The Lanthanoids', which covers (I)(ii) and the 2-mark part (II) — 3 of the 5 marks. Within the row, (I)(i) alloys is 'General Properties of the Transition Elements (d-Block)' and the 1-mark part (III) is 'Some Important Compounds of Transition Elements'.

questions.stem:
(I) Give reasons :
(i) Aniline on nitration gives good amount of m-nitroaniline, though \(-\mathrm{NH_2}\) group is o/p directing in electrophilic substitution reactions.
(ii) \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_2\,NH}\) is more basic than \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3N}\) in an aqueous solution.
(iii) Ammonolysis of alkyl halides is not a good method to prepare pure primary amines.
(II) Write the reaction involved in the following :
(i) Carbyl amine test
(ii) Gabriel phthalimide synthesis
questions._flag: The printed marks are '3 + 2'. Filed on 'Chemical Reactions of Amines', which covers all of the 3-mark part (I) and (II)(i); (II)(ii) the Gabriel phthalimide synthesis belongs to 'Preparation of Amines'.

questions.stem:
(I) Write the structures of A, B and C in the following reactions :
(i) \(\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^-} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{CuCN}} \mathrm{A} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H_2O/H^+}} \mathrm{B} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\mathrm{NH_3}} \mathrm{C}\)
(ii) \(\mathrm{C_6H_5NO_2} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Fe/HCl}} \mathrm{A} \xrightarrow[273\ \mathrm{K}]{\mathrm{NaNO_2 + HCl}} \mathrm{B} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}} \mathrm{C}\)
(II) Why aniline does not undergo Friedal-Crafts reaction ?
(III) Arrange the following in increasing order of their boiling point :
\(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}\), \(\mathrm{C_2H_5NH_2}\), \(\mathrm{(C_2H_5)_3N}\)
questions._flag: Part (II) is printed 'Friedal-Crafts' — a misspelling of Friedel-Crafts. Transcribed as printed, not corrected; the answer is unaffected. Both schemes in (I) draw their starting material as a skeletal benzene ring carrying \(-\mathrm{N_2^+Cl^-}\) and \(-\mathrm{NO_2}\) respectively; each names one compound without loss and each scheme is a straight linear chain, so they are written inline and no figure is requested. The printed marks are '3 + 1 + 1': the 3-mark part (I) is diazonium chemistry in both schemes, so the row is filed on 'Chemical Reactions of Diazonium Salts', while (II) and (III) are 'Chemical Reactions of Amines'.
